case.summary: Verdict: legitimate at probability 0.03, pattern none. The episode is the single flagged transaction 3506725 ($1,000.03 online, product R) on card C10434-K1; exposure is $0.00 since no fraud was found. Decisive evidence spanned two families: memory (cms_p/cal_p of 0.02 from the case-memory calibration, sharply contradicting the raw 0.90 risk_score, plus a weak prior cleared alert CC-0873 on this same card) and history/device (the purchase sat in the card's modal home region with 24 prior visits, card_testing_check and under_threshold_burst both came back empty, and the new device profile was explicitly not strong so it carries no shared-origin weight). Because this was a single-signal risk-score alert below 0.70 (R1), we requested customer_validation before considering any block rather than acting on the score alone; the assumed reply was a confirmation that the customer recognized the $1,000.03 charge from a new device, which settled the question under R3. The bank's action now is auto-route: keep the case open for the record (CREATE_CASE), ALLOW_TRANSACTION, and CLOSE_NO_FRAUD with the confirmation noted — no L1/L2 approval needed. An analyst re-reading this could reasonably worry the size jump (prior max $670.04) plus a first-use device still looks like early-stage card-not-present fraud (similar closed cases CC-3954, CC-4362, CC-2720, CC-3549 all confirmed card_not_present_new_device fraud on structurally similar device profiles); had the customer instead denied the charge, R2 would have applied (BLOCK_CARD at L1, CREATE_CASE) since exposure would stay ≤ $2,500.
